Laura / Marissa — answers and artifacts below. TL;DR: we can meet EuroCap's EU-only residency requirements for hosted accounts and provide a signed bridge letter for the audit window. Details: 

1) Topology for EU-hosted customers (this account)
   - Inference endpoints: eu-central-1 (Frankfurt).
   - Object storage (primary): eu-central-1; automated backups retained in eu-west-1 (Ireland) by default. No automatic replication to US regions for backup copies on this account.
   - Backups: scheduled daily snapshots — for customers that require stricter residency we can enable single-region retention (no replication) and provide a configuration change before onboarding.

2) Control-plane logs / telemetry
   - Our multi-tenant control plane processes metadata in our control region (currently US-based). Metadata includes request-level metrics (latency, token counts) but not raw customer content. For customers with EU residency requirements we offer two options:
      a) Dedicated: keep control-plane telemetry and logs in-region (EU) as part of the Dedicated deployment.
      b) Hosted with export restrictions: we can disable non-essential telemetry collection and provide a contract addendum that limits telemetry export; however some platform-level operational logs (alerting) may still route to our central incident system. We can provide a technical appendix documenting which telemetry fields are exported.

3) KMS & keys
   - Customer-managed keys: supported via Azure Key Vault (eu-region) or AWS KMS in eu-central-1. Keys can be provisioned and bound to the customer's storage encryption.

4) SOC 2 / bridge letter
   - Compliance confirms we have a Type II report covering 2025 (report covers 2025-01-01 through 2025-12-31). That leaves an audit-window mismatch for Oct 2025 - Sep 2026.
   - We can produce a signed bridge letter from our Head of Security that explicitly states controls remained in place from 2026-01-01 through 2026-09-30 and references the 2025 Type II report. Draft attached.
   - Estimated turnaround: 2 business days for a draft from Security, 1 additional day for legal review and signature (subject to legal queue).
